title: Work IQ: agents can execute reusable recipes
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and correctly distinguishes documented Work IQ controls from unpublished recipe details. The two Graph grant and provisioning calls need only minor formatting corrections: move their request-body properties into the control notes.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: Work IQ API enablement
claims.claim: No admin-centre UI control is documented for provisioning the Work IQ resource service principal.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ enable API organization service principal Entra admin center UI create enterprise application fdcc1f02; read enable-work-iq and Entra portal service-principal results; Work IQ steps use Graph Explorer or Azure CLI, not an admin-centre control.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: Work IQ API enablement
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions the tenant's Work IQ resource.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7"
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call and its rendered call to 'POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals'. Add the note 'The request body sets appId to fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7.' Keep the existing documentation link.

claims.claim: An app's Work IQ admin consent is granted in Microsoft Entra admin center at Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: Grant consent: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants grants tenant-wide delegated consent using clientId, consentType AllPrincipals, resourceId and the WorkIQAgent.Ask scope.
claims.quote: The consentType is AllPrincipals, indicating that you're consenting on behalf of all users in the tenant. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and its rendered call to 'POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants'. Add to the note: 'The request body sets clientId to the client service principal object ID, consentType to AllPrincipals, resourceId to the Work IQ service principal object ID, and scope to WorkIQAgent.Ask. Revoke with DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{grant-id}.' Keep the existing Graph documentation link. The cited Create oAuth2PermissionGrant reference confirms the body properties, and the Work IQ admin-consent page confirms the scope.

claims.claim: DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{grant-id} revokes the specified delegated permission grant object.
claims.quote: To revoke all grants, send a DELETE request to the oauth2PermissionGrant object. ... DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/47nZsM8O_UuNq5Jz3QValETpqX7OcT1EgRxx6AR7VXqdkr0_VoxiRIUeDrmns6Kl

claims.claim: On the same app's API permissions page, administrators can select WorkIQAgent.Ask and Revoke admin consent.
claims.quote: Revoke consent: On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.claim: Existing tokens remain valid until they expire after admin consent is revoked.
claims.quote: Existing tokens remain valid until they expire; no new tokens can be issued after revocation.

claims.claim: Deleting an oauth2PermissionGrant object revokes all permissions held in that object.
claims.quote: To revoke one or more grants, run a PATCH request on the oauth2PermissionGrant object and specify only the delegated permissions to retain in the scope parameter. To revoke all grants, send a DELETE request to the oauth2PermissionGrant object.
